title: Graceful mid-period quota reconciliation for reserved→hosted tenant migrations
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: Customers moving from Reserved capacity (Dedicated pools) to Hosted tiers often change quota models mid-billing-period. Current reset and reconciliation logic assumes cutovers at month/day boundaries or full-epoch handoffs, which leads to two problem classes: 1) double-charging or lost credits when leases overlap and both systems bill for the same tokens; 2) opaque provisional throttles during migration that cause customer-facing errors.

Goal: Provide a deterministic, auditable mid-period migration reconciliation approach that: preserves customer credit/prorations, prevents transient over-consumption, maintains SLA guardrails, and allows safe automated cutover without manual billing intervention.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change pricing tiers or introduce new customer-visible billing line items. It focuses on ledger correctness and quota enforcement during a migration flow.

Proposed design summary:
- Introduce a migration-safe cutover protocol that uses a short-lived authoritative snapshot (the "migration-snapshot") of tenant usage and lease state at T_cutover (ISO8601, tenant TZ-aware). The snapshot is stored in the tenant ledger service as an immutable record.
- During cutover window (configurable, default 5 minutes) both Reserved and Hosted metering continue but are evaluated with a reconciliation policy: any Hosted tokens consumed that can be mapped to a Reserved pending request are marked as "reclaimed" on the Reserved ledger rather than double-counted.
- Create a deterministic mapping layer that associates API keys / route hashes to the migration snapshot using API-key aliases. This prevents ambiguity when customers rotate keys during cutover.
- Compute prorated quota allowances for the remainder of the period: remaining_reserved_quota_at_T = reserved_quota_total - committed_usage_snapshot. Convert remaining_reserved_quota_at_T to hosted_quota with a one-time transfer record (ledger credit) with unique idempotency key.
- Enforcement: while reconciliation is in progress, apply a soft throttle (95th percentile latency-friendly) for tokens above the transferred allowance and surface explicit reason codes in rate-limit responses (X-Quota-Reconciliation: migrating).
- Auditing and billing: emit reconciliation records to billing-export downstream with reconciliation_reason=migration and include before/after snapshots for invoice generation and customer support.

Telemetry and correctness checks:
- Metrics to emit: reconciliation.duration_ms, reconciliation.mapped_tokens, reconciliation.unmatched_tokens, migration.snapshot_size, reconciliation.idempotency_conflicts.
- Validation job: nightly job that cross-checks migration snapshots against downstream billing exports to flag >0.05% token discrepancies for human review.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Key rotation mid-window: resolved by alias map; if rotation is faster than snapshot propagation, operations may need to extend cutover window.
- Long-lived streaming requests crossing T_cutover: we treat the streaming request as belonging to the origin system that accepted the first token; follow-up tokens are reconciled via KV-cache ownership marker. This avoids tearing the stream mid-request.
- Clock skew across regions: use server-side authoritative monotonic time and include tenant TZ context for human-readable audit lines.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement migration-snapshot API and ledger transfer record (server-side feature flag).
2) Canary with internal test tenant migrating between reserved→hosted within a single region. Validate reconciliation metrics and exported invoices.
3) Open beta to selected customers with 24/7 oncall coverage and rollback plan.
4) Full launch and add automation to the console migration wizard.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for idempotent ledger-transfer creation.
- Integration test for key-rotation and stream continuity.
- E2E simulation harness that replays production traffic at 10% QPS to validate mapping heuristics.

Rollback: Reconciliation writes are idempotent and reversible via a compensating transfer record; we will add a safe-read-only mode for 48 hours post-cutover before releasing the transfer to billing exports to allow manual rollback in case of anomalies.

Ownership: Billing infra owns ledger transfer and exports. Serving runtime implements soft-throttle and alias mapping hooks. PM/Console will own UX and migration orchestration.
